description: Fetch one Handshakr supplier an AI agent may read, by slug. `contactable` says whether the supplier has switched agent access on and may be approached. `description` and `category` are the company's own words or null; text Handshakr wrote from public sources is in `handshakr_summary` / `handshakr_category`, labelled, and is not a fact about the company. `trust_score` is null: no score is computed. `trading_name_of`, when not null, names the registered company this listing is a trading name of (legal name, company number, the passport holding its Companies House record): listings that share a company number there are one company, not several. `verifiable_record` is the latest signed, append-only version of the public passport: its version, sha256, log position, and where to fetch the W3C Verifiable Credential and its status. `classification` is the register's three classifications: { what_they_do, who_its_for, delivery } each { slug, top_slug, name, method, method_label, source } or null with `unknown_reason` saying why, and `taxonomy_version`; `method` is supplier, label, sic (Companies House SIC code) or website (their own website text, not reviewed). `register_checks` lists what public sources said on a date (DNS, TLS, security.txt, GLEIF, ICO, SEC EDGAR): observations, not claims; `not_checked` means nothing observed yet, and sanctions appear only as `no_match` against all four lists. Each is null when it could not be read.
